newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Thousands crowd Afghan-Pakistan border crossing.
newsitem.headline: Thousands crowd Afghan-Pakistan border crossing.

text.p: Pakistani guards fired shots in the air on Monday to deter a crowd of Afghans trying to storm the gates at the Afghan-Pakistan border crossing, witnesses said.
They said thousands of people were crowding the gates on both sides and Afghans could be seen trekking into Pakistan from nearby mountains where there were no border guards to stop them.
A Red Cross food convoy bound for Kabul was halted as Pakistani officials refused to open the gates for fear it would be rushed by the crowds.

The convoy of 35 lorries, carrying some 20 tonnes of food and medical equipment, organised by the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), had left the northwestern Pakistani town of Peshawar early in the morning but had been unable to cross by late afternoon.
ICRC relief administrator Robert McKay told reporters at Torkham that he was trying to contact the Pakistani interior and foreign ministries for help.
"But the situation is not clear yet," he said.
The convoy was carrying wheat flour, rice, cooking oil, blankets and medical equipment. ICRC officials said their organisation had sufficient stocks of medicines in Kabul.

Pakistan closed the border earlier this month to stop a fresh wave of Afghan refugees fleeing from fighting in eastern Afghanistan where the Taleban Islamic militia captured three provinces before taking Kabul on Friday.
